answer: A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 4 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. The cedar chain is verified at intake and copper publishes each anchor. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 4 epochs old, anchored at a echo checkpoint. That bill is paid per identity, so 229 aliases cost 331 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
